children: Australian stocks are poised to keep falling at the start of the week, following U.S. equities deeper into the red. ASX futures are down by 0.6% ahead of Monday's session, suggesting that the S&P/ASX 200 will add to the 6.1% decline compiled across what is already its longest losing streak since April. The benchmark index has fallen for seven straight sessions and is coming off its worst week since June 2022. Some investors will be waiting on the midweek release of October inflation data, which may provide clues about the path for the economy and interest rates. In the U.S. on Friday, all three major indices rounded out their worst weeks since March 2020. The DJIA and S&P 500 fell 1.9% and 3.7%, respectively, for the day and both entered correction territory. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
